description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and various accuracy metrics, including Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, with a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, and tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis represents Accuracy, with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy (blue, solid line), Δ Accuracy (orange, dashed line), and Initial Accuracy (green, dash-dot line). The Final Accuracy line remains relatively stable, starting at approximately 0.9 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86 and ending at around 0.95 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00, with a peak of 0.96 at an Initial Confidence of 0.98. The Δ Accuracy line starts at around 0.35 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86, decreases to a minimum of approximately 0.05 at an Initial Confidence of 0.95, and then increases slightly to around 0.1 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00. The Initial Accuracy line begins at approximately 0.7 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86, increases to a peak of around 0.93 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, and then decreases to approximately 0.75 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00.
